I read all of lines 1-315. The file has no @[simp] declarations and no local simp sets, so it can't contain a cycle, competing rules or unwanted expansion. The only `simp only` call is inside the two commutation proofs. It clears terms of the form (p*p-p)*q using sub_self, zero_mul and mul_zero, and it is safe and terminating.

I looked for missing canonical simp lemmas and found no justified case:
- `cfc_sin_angleOperatorC` (cfc sin (angleOperatorC U V) = sinAngleOperatorC U V) is the only rewrite lemma for the angle. It is used only through explicit `rw [← cfc_sin_angleOperatorC, ...]` in this file (line 160) and in TanAngleFunctionalCalculus.lean (line 233). Those rewrites run in the reverse direction to insert the sine, which is deliberate and not what simp would do. Tagging it @[simp] would not help those uses and could interfere with them.
- `angleOperatorC` and `cosAngleOperatorC` are unfolded by `rw [angleOperatorC]` or `rw [cosAngleOperatorC]`. I saw no uses where simp needed an unfolding lemma.
- `adjoint_starProjection_sub` is stated with `.adjoint`. It is used only as a one-off `rw` inside hgram. I found no Mathlib simp lemma for the adjoint of a starProjection to conflict with it, and it has no other uses.

I did not check the imported files OperatorAngleComplex and OperatorAngleReal for simp lemmas about sinAngleOperatorC. Everything else is a proof-structure or duplication question, which is outside this rubric.
